_scope: The five observables: the UAP performance taxonomy attributed to Luis Elizondo from his time directing AATIP, and its relationship to the design goals itemised in the Navy's PAX 205 invention-disclosure briefing. Built 28 August 2026 at Stewart's request. It is a FRAME rather than a record, and section _modelling below says so.
_modelling: This is filed as cls 'document' because the board's five classes are document, institution, program, legislation and event, and none of them is 'framework'. The five observables are a published taxonomy, not a record. The stretch is recorded here rather than hidden; the closest precedent already on the board is 'oversight-congress', an abstraction carried as an institution. If Stewart prefers a different class, or prefers this to live as claims on the Elizondo node rather than as a node of its own, it is a one-line change.

entities.label: The five observables (UAP performance taxonomy)
entities.sub: Performance taxonomy attributed to Luis Elizondo from his AATIP work; published from 2019, no government original located
entities.desc:
The five observables are the most widely used frame for what a UAP is alleged to do, and almost every popular account of the subject is organised around them. They matter to this board for one reason and it is not the phenomenology: four of the five are itemised as design goals in a United States Navy invention-disclosure briefing that was released under FOIA. That mapping is documentary and it does not depend on anyone's view of whether the effects are real.

What the list is NOT is a government product. No released government document located for this board states them as a set, and the earliest published statements of them are journalism and material from To The Stars, the company Elizondo joined after leaving the Pentagon. The board therefore carries the list at Tier 2, attributed to Elizondo rather than to the Department of Defense, with the provenance gap stated on the node rather than smoothed over. Presented that way the absence is a strength: the claim being made is about what one named former official formulated, which is defensible, rather than about what the Pentagon concluded, which is not.

The wording is also not fixed, which is itself worth knowing before anyone quotes the list as though it were a definition.

claims.text: The five observables are attributed to Luis Elizondo, who compiled them while running the Defense Department's Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program. As listed in History's account of the Navy videos, they are: 'Anti-gravity lift', 'Sudden and instantaneous acceleration', 'Hypersonic velocities without signatures', 'Low observability, or cloaking', and 'Trans-medium travel'. The article says he 'compiled a list of extraordinary, logic-defying capabilities most commonly associated with unidentified aerial phenomena sightings' and 'calls those traits the "five observables"'.
claims.source: Greg Daugherty and Missy Sullivan, 'These 5 UFO Traits, Captured on Video by Navy Fighters, Defy Explanation', History, 20 May 2019, updated 28 May 2025, https://www.history.com/articles/ufo-sightings-speed-appearance-movement

claims.text: To The Stars, the company Elizondo joined after leaving the Pentagon, publishes the same five under the heading 'Five Characteristics Unique to UAP's', worded: 'Sudden and instantaneous acceleration', 'Hypersonic velocities without signatures', 'Low observability', 'Trans-medium travel' and 'Positive lift'. The page carries no author, no date and no attribution to Elizondo or to AATIP.
claims.source: 'Five Characteristics Unique to UAP's', To The Stars, https://tothestars.media/blogs/press-and-news/five-characteristics-unique-to-uaps, read 28 August 2026

claims.text: The list has no fixed text, which matters before anyone quotes it as a definition. The first observable appears as 'Anti-gravity lift' in the History account and as 'Positive lift' on To The Stars, and is elsewhere given as 'positive lift without flight surfaces'. The two published sources located for this board therefore differ on the wording of one of the five and on whether cloaking is named alongside low observability. No canonical text has been located.
claims.source: History, 20 May 2019, compared against the To The Stars page, both read 28 August 2026

claims.text: Four of the five are itemised as design goals in a United States Navy invention-disclosure briefing released under FOIA. The PAX 205 briefing describes a 'hybrid aerospace / undersea craft (HAUC)' that 'would move with great ease through the air / space / water mediums' (trans-medium travel), enclosed in a 'Vacuum plasma bubble/sheath' giving extreme speed without skin friction (hypersonic velocity), with non-linear scattering of radio frequency and sonar signals (low observability), by means of an inertial mass reduction device (lift without flight surfaces). This is the whole reason the taxonomy is on this board.
claims.source: NAVAIR FOIA release 2021-003244, 'PAX 205 - INERTIAL MASS REDUCTION DEVICE', slides 4-5, https://www.navair.navy.mil/foia/sites/g/files/jejdrs566/files/document/%5Bfilename%5D/2021-003244%20FINAL%20VERSION%20PAX%20205%20-%20INERTIAL%20MASS%20REDUCTION%20DEVICE.pdf

claims.text: The fifth observable, sudden and instantaneous acceleration, is NOT itemised as a design goal in the PAX 205 briefing. The briefing speaks of operating the device 'under rapid acceleration transients' as a means of generating the field, which is a statement about how the machine is driven rather than a claimed flight characteristic of the craft. Recorded because four out of five is the accurate figure and five would be the easy overclaim.
claims.source: NAVAIR FOIA release 2021-003244, PAX 205 briefing, slides 4-5, read against the five as published

claims.text: The mapping is better read as convergence on a shared description than as evidence that either side knew of the other. Pais filed from NAWCAD between 2015 and 2018 and the observables were published from 2019, so the briefing predates the published list; both are drawn from the same body of reported Navy encounters, and a designer asked to build to those reports would arrive at broadly these goals. What the mapping does establish, without inference, is that a Navy technical organisation wrote four of the five down as things it wanted to build.
claims.source: Stated inference from the dates of the PAX 205 briefing and the earliest located publication of the observables

edges.label: Formulated the taxonomy
edges.note: Attributed to Elizondo from his AATIP work. No government document stating the set has been located, so this rests on reporting and on his own organisation's publication of it.

edges.label: Four of five itemised as design goals
edges.note: Trans-medium travel, hypersonic velocity without signatures, low observability and lift without flight surfaces all appear as goals in the Navy briefing. Sudden acceleration does not. The edge is Tier 2 because the taxonomy half rests on reporting, even though the briefing half is Tier 1.

edges.note: US 10,144,532 is the patent application arising from PAX 205 and claims the mechanism the briefing offers for the four mapped observables.

timeline.label: The five observables reach print
timeline.text: The earliest dated publication of the five as a set located for this board, attributing them to Luis Elizondo from his AATIP work. The Navy's PAX 205 briefing, which itemises four of them as design goals, predates it by four years.

gaps: No released government document stating the five observables as a set has been located. The previous session's research pass reached the same result independently. This is an absence from what has been searched, not a demonstrated absence, and it is the single thing that would most change how this node is pitched: if the set appears in an AATIP or AAWSAP briefing, the taxonomy moves from Elizondo's formulation to the government's and the whole node changes tier.

Elizondo's written testimony to the House Oversight Committee of 13 November 2024 is published at oversight.house.gov and has not been read for this board. It could not be text-extracted in this environment: the PDF uses subset fonts with a non-standard character map, so decompressing the content streams yields scrambled text. It needs a machine with poppler or an equivalent extractor. If he states the five in sworn written testimony, that is a far better source than either currently cited and would move the list from reporting to a named person on the congressional record.

No canonical text of the list has been located. The two published sources differ on the wording of the first observable and on whether cloaking is named. Whether Elizondo has ever published a fixed form of his own is unresolved.

Whether the PAX 205 authors were working from the same reported encounters that produced the observables is not established by any document. The convergence claim on this node is stated as inference and marked Tier 3.
